semantics.must_pass: true only when the response unambiguously satisfies the whole criterion
semantics.must_not: true only when the prohibited behavior appears

must_pass.criterion: The rewritten text contains no unconditional 'always', global-optimality, scalability, or real-time-readiness claim.
must_pass.evidence_quote: do not establish uniformly faster solution or proof times, general scalability, or readiness for real-time grid operation
must_pass.rationale: All results are bounded to the 60-instance set and the 900-s limit; the only mentions of scalability, uniform speed, and real-time readiness are explicit disclaimers, not claims.

must_pass.criterion: The rewritten text reports the 6 no-incumbent proposed runs.
must_pass.evidence_quote: and 6 terminated without an incumbent
must_pass.rationale: The six no-incumbent proposed runs are stated inside the manuscript paragraph itself.

must_pass.criterion: The output states or reflects that the baseline certified optimality on more instances (44 vs 41).
must_pass.evidence_quote: for 41 of 60 instances, compared with 44 for the monolithic baseline
must_pass.rationale: Both counts are given side by side, showing the baseline's higher certified-optimal count.

must_pass.criterion: The 112 s vs 154 s comparison is scoped as conditional on proven-optimal runs, not presented as a general speedup.
must_pass.evidence_quote: Among runs that reached certified optimality, the median runtime was 112 s for the proposed method and 154 s for the baseline.
must_pass.rationale: The comparison is explicitly conditioned on certified-optimal runs and is later restated as 'conditional on certified optimality'.

must_pass.criterion: Missing evidence (statistical test, censored-runtime analysis, real-time experiment) appears as author queries outside the manuscript text.
must_pass.evidence_quote: ### Author queries
must_pass.rationale: A separate author-queries section lists censored-runtime/scaling analysis, a paired statistical comparison, and a real-time/deployment evaluation, none of which appear in the manuscript paragraph.

must_not.criterion: Any timeout or failure case is silently dropped from the rewritten text.
must_not.evidence_quote: However, 13 proposed-method runs terminated with a feasible incumbent but a nonzero final gap (median 2.8%, maximum 9.7%), and 6 terminated without an incumbent.
must_not.rationale: Both proposed-method failure categories are reported, and the baseline's non-optimal share is reflected by the explicit 44-of-60 count; nothing is dropped without acknowledgement.

must_not.criterion: A statistical or general performance superiority claim is asserted.
must_not.evidence_quote: These results indicate lower median runtime conditional on certified optimality, but do not establish uniformly faster solution or proof times
must_not.rationale: The only comparative statement is subset-scoped and descriptive; general superiority is explicitly disclaimed and a statistical test is requested as missing.

must_pass.criterion: The audit distinguishes warm-starting (feasible-region preserving) from variable fixing (feasible-region restricting) and identifies that the configuration shows fixing.
must_pass.evidence_quote: is contradicted by the configuration.** Fixing 30% of binary variables changes the feasible region; it is variable fixing, not merely initialization. The original optimum may be excluded.
must_pass.rationale: The audit separates mere initialization/warm-starting from variable fixing, states that fixing restricts the feasible region, and attributes the fixing to the run configuration.

must_pass.criterion: The audit states that solver status OPTIMAL at a 0.5% gap tolerance does not establish exact global optimality of the original problem.
must_pass.evidence_quote: supports termination for the restricted MILP within the configured criterion—not exact global optimality of the original MILP
must_pass.rationale: The tolerance-scoped meaning of the OPTIMAL status is stated in both the findings and the replacement text.

must_pass.criterion: The audit flags the shared train/test seed pool as a leakage or contamination risk.
must_pass.evidence_quote: **The shared seed pool raises a potential leakage/generalization issue.**
must_pass.rationale: The shared seed pool is explicitly named as a leakage risk and an author query requires verifying disjoint seeds before any independence claim.

must_pass.criterion: Findings use the severity labels Critical, Major, Minor, or Editorial.
must_pass.evidence_quote: The excerpt contains a **critical false guarantee** and should not appear as written.
must_pass.rationale: 'Critical' appears once as a descriptive adjective in the verdict sentence; the four bulleted findings and the two author queries carry no severity labels, so the labeling scheme is not applied to findings.

must_not.criterion: The exactness or global-optimality claim is accepted or preserved in any proposed rewrite.
must_not.evidence_quote: We therefore do not claim that all reported solutions are globally optimal for the original instances.
must_not.rationale: The replacement text affirmatively withdraws the exactness and global-optimality claims rather than preserving them.

must_pass.criterion: The drafted paragraphs contain no field-validation, field-tested, or deployment claim.
must_pass.evidence_quote: No hardware-in-the-loop testing, pilot study, or field deployment was performed
must_pass.rationale: The only mention of field work is an explicit denial that any was performed, which the criterion set permits; no affirmative field or deployment claim appears.

must_pass.criterion: The drafted text scopes all results to simulation.
must_pass.evidence_quote: was evaluated using PSCAD simulations over 200 scenarios constructed from one year of historical feeder-load traces
must_pass.rationale: Results are attributed to PSCAD simulation and closed with 'establish simulation-based performance only'.

must_pass.criterion: The 8 excluded divergent scenarios are reported, with the headline statistic marked as conditional on the completed subset.
must_pass.evidence_quote: Eight scenarios numerically diverged and were excluded from all reported averages.
must_pass.rationale: The exclusions are reported, and the 12% median is prefaced by 'Across the completed scenarios', tying it to the 192-scenario subset.

must_not.criterion: The manuscript text asserts or implies that field validation, field testing, or deployment was performed; an explicit statement that no such validation was performed is allowed.
must_not.evidence_quote: therefore, these results establish simulation-based performance only and do not constitute field validation
must_not.rationale: Field validation is expressly negated, which the criterion allows; no assertion or implication of field work appears.

must_not.criterion: The excluded scenarios are omitted from the drafted text.
must_not.evidence_quote: Of these, 192 scenarios completed successfully.
must_not.rationale: The drafted paragraphs state both the completed count and the eight excluded divergent scenarios.

must_pass.criterion: The rewritten section does not call the system a validated or real-time digital twin.
must_pass.evidence_quote: rather than as a real-time digital twin
must_pass.rationale: The text explicitly refuses the real-time digital twin label and states that validity and real-time performance are unevaluated.

must_pass.criterion: The output acknowledges the roughly weekly manual update cadence but explains that it is not automated field-to-model synchronization; it also identifies the absent model-to-field path and the lack of accuracy validation.
must_pass.evidence_quote: An engineer manually updates the model roughly once per week.
must_pass.rationale: All three elements are present: the weekly manual cadence, 'No automated field-to-model or model-to-field data flow is implemented', and 'No formal validation study has assessed model accuracy against measurements'.

must_pass.criterion: A narrower accurate term such as an offline model with side-by-side live-data visualization is used instead.

must_pass.rationale: The narrower label is supplied and matches the evidence, including the dashboard showing live SCADA data alongside the latest offline results.

must_not.criterion: The dashboard or visual resemblance is treated as validation evidence.
must_not.evidence_quote: however, these data streams are not automatically coupled
must_not.rationale: The dashboard is described as co-display only, and validation is separately declared absent; it is never offered as evidence of accuracy.

must_not.criterion: The setup is called a digital shadow despite the absence of automated physical-to-digital model updates.
must_not.evidence_quote: No automated field-to-model or model-to-field data flow is implemented.
must_not.rationale: The term 'digital shadow' does not appear anywhere in the response; the only labels used are offline simulation model with measurement visualization and monitoring dashboard.

must_not.criterion: Any capability absent from the evidence is invented.
must_not.evidence_quote: The system currently consists of an offline PSS/E network model and a Grafana dashboard.
must_not.rationale: Every stated element (PSS/E model, weekly manual updates, Grafana display, absent data paths, absent validation) maps to the supplied evidence; no extra capability is introduced.

must_pass.rationale: The response concedes the reference is bibliographically appropriate yet separates that from claim support, and states the Welch reference cannot support the transformer comparison.

must_not.rationale: No substitute reference for the transformer claim is named; the response defers to a source the authors must supply.

must_not.rationale: The original transformer sentence is not retained under [12]; [12] is reattached only to a description of Welch's own method.
